help.title: Help Center
help.intro: Step-by-step guidance for features available in your application.
help.offline: Built into JENESIS: works without an internet connection.
help.no_guarantees: This guidance is not accounting, tax, security or legal advice.

start.title: First steps
start.intro: Choose the right entry point before you sign in.
start.step1: Open the Seller (red), Administrator (blue) or Network & Maintenance (green) shortcut. A user must have the appropriate role for that application.
start.step2: On a new installation, complete the setup screen: enter your company, country, base currency and a strong administrator password. There is no supplied default password.
start.step3: Sign in with your own username. Use the left menu to open a module; switch languages from the top bar. Sign out when leaving the computer.

company.title: Companies and people
company.intro: Company data is separated by membership, not by trusting a request header.
company.step1: In Settings, edit the company details, or create another company if your role allows it. A new company gets its own chart of accounts, not another company’s balances.
company.step2: Choose the country and base currency when creating the company. Supported base currencies are XAF, RWF, USD, EUR and UGX; changing the existing base currency is blocked to avoid reinterpreting old amounts.
company.step3: In Settings → Users, create a separate account and role for each person. Assign company access explicitly; switch companies with the top-bar selector to confirm you are in the right ledger.

contacts.title: Customers and suppliers
contacts.intro: Contact records belong to one company.
contacts.step1: Open Customers, then use Add customer. Enter a name and any available contact details. Open a row to edit; check the message if a save is refused.
contacts.step2: In the Administrator application, use Suppliers → Add supplier for purchase partners. Seller accounts do not receive supplier data.
contacts.step3: Deactivation hides a contact from new activity but keeps its existing invoices and history. Aging tabs require report permission.

products.title: Products and stock
products.intro: Selling price and inventory cost are different fields.
products.step1: In Administrator → Inventory, add a product with a unique SKU, name, selling price and cost price. Edit it there; stock changes are recorded through purchases, sales or authorized adjustments.
products.step2: Seller → Inventory shows a catalog with available quantity and selling price, not purchase cost or inventory valuation. Low-stock warnings come from your company’s inventory.
products.step3: Check the stock movements before an adjustment. A posted sales invoice affects inventory and the ledger; do not delete historical postings to change quantities.

sales.title: Sales workflow
sales.intro: An invoice is not the same thing as a cash receipt.
sales.step1: Open Sales → Invoices and create an invoice. Select the customer, dates and product lines; review quantity, selling price, discount and tax before saving.
sales.step2: Auto-post creates the associated accounting and stock movements. If you save as a draft, review it and post deliberately. A second post is refused.
sales.step3: Use the payment action to record settlement; partial payment is tracked. Print a copy for the customer after checking its status and totals.
sales.step4: Quotes and orders are separate stages. Use a credit note for an approved return or correction; confirm whether to put items back into stock.

purchases.title: Purchasing workflow
purchases.intro: Available to authorized Administrator roles, not Seller.
purchases.step1: Create the supplier first. In Purchases → Bills, select the supplier, dates, vendor reference and product lines with costs and tax.
purchases.step2: Review the bill before auto-posting or manually post a saved draft. Posting updates the ledger and applicable stock; repeating the same post does not duplicate it.
purchases.step3: Record payments separately. Review purchase orders and returns in their tabs and check supplier balances before closing a period.

banking.title: Bank and cash
banking.intro: Cash and bank records are company-specific.
banking.step1: In Banking, review accounts and the current balance before entering a payment or transfer. Choose the correct company and reference.
banking.step2: Match the payment to its invoice or bill where possible. Check whether it is partial or complete and verify the resulting balance.
banking.step3: Reconcile against an external bank statement outside the app; do not treat the screen balance as proof the bank has settled a transfer.

accounting.title: Double-entry accounting
accounting.intro: A posted journal must have equal debits and credits.
accounting.step1: In Accounting, open the chart of accounts and choose accounts that belong to the current company. Never treat a display-only translation of an account name as a new account.
accounting.step2: For a manual journal, supply the date, description and lines. Verify debits equal credits before posting. Posted entries cannot be silently edited.
accounting.step3: Correct a posting with a documented reversal rather than deleting evidence. Recheck the trial balance and audit trail after the correction.

reports.title: Reports and checks
reports.intro: Reports reflect data posted in the selected company.
reports.step1: Open Reports to view a trial balance or financial summary. Compare the reporting period and currency against your source documents.
reports.step2: If totals look wrong, check whether invoices or bills remain drafts, whether payments were recorded and whether a company switch changed the active ledger.
reports.step3: Only authorized roles can see full financial reports and contact aging. Exported numbers still require review by an accountant.

backup.title: Backup and restore
backup.intro: There are two different safeguards: a company JSON export and a full host SQLite safety copy.
backup.step1: In Administrator → Settings → Backup, download the company export and store a second copy outside the computer. Check the filename and date. This export excludes passwords and sessions.
backup.step2: Before a restore, check the chosen company and file. Enter your administrator password and type RESTORE exactly. Validation checks checksum, company ownership, references and balanced journals before the transaction runs.
backup.step3: The service creates a verified full-database safety copy before writing; a successful company restore signs everyone out. Sign in again and verify invoices, balances and stock.
backup.step4: For a full-database disaster recovery, close the application first and get a trusted technician to restore a verified SQLite snapshot. Do not move only the .db file while the service is running.

network.title: Health and maintenance
network.intro: The green application checks the local service. It does not provide a business ledger to maintenance staff.
network.step1: Sign in with a Network role (or as administrator). Use Run health check to inspect service status, SQLite integrity and foreign-key enforcement.
network.step2: Use Create verified snapshot to make a consistent full SQLite copy in the host’s backups folder. Record the name; copy it to separate storage using authorized operating-system access.
network.step3: Only an administrator can download a company export or restore one here. A Network user cannot see products, customers, accounts or financial reports.
network.step4: LAN hosting is off by default. After first-run setup on the host, use the Network application to enable HTTPS hosting. Give clients its Seller or Administrator browser address; all users sign in to the host’s one database. Never share or sync live SQLite files.
network.step5: Read the SHA-256 certificate fingerprint from the host’s own Network window. On each client, compare it using a separate trusted channel before accepting the self-signed certificate; never accept a mismatch. Keep the host powered on and backed up. Firewalls may need TCP 34671 opened only for the private network; public Internet access is forbidden.

safety.title: Passwords and safe operation
safety.intro: Keep a secure copy of credentials and backups separate from the workstation.
safety.step1: Do not share accounts or passwords. After failed sign-ins, access may be temporarily locked. Use the authorized recovery procedure if the only administrator loses access.
safety.step2: Before updating or uninstalling, make a backup and verify that the current database can be read. Installed data is in the user data folder, not the program folder.
safety.step3: Use the same application backend for all three modes. Never open the live SQLite file in another program to edit it while JENESIS is running.

limits.title: Current limitations
limits.intro: JENESIS 0.1 is an early, unsigned release. Verify results before relying on them.
limits.step1: Supported currencies are separate company base currencies, not automatic exchange conversion. There is no proven historical FX revaluation or conversion in this release.
limits.step2: Private LAN browser clients can connect by HTTPS only after a local operator opts in. A remote installed desktop/client mode, Internet access, automatic off-site backups and unattended disaster recovery are not provided. Never copy or sync a live database to another PC; keep manual external backups.
limits.step3: An installer test on a Windows CI runner is not a physical-PC, upgrade, antivirus or offline-installation certification. Consult an accountant for legal tax and reporting obligations.
limits.step4: For XAF, RWF and UGX, fractional monetary amounts are refused instead of being hidden by a zero-decimal display. Adjust the source transaction with accounting approval; no country-specific rounding policy has been certified.
